# NOTES ON THE TEXT (two books; keep separate)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE CLOCK STRUCK ONE (Fergus Hume, 1898, Gutenberg 55689)

**Front matter:** Warne & Co., London/New York 1898. Author of "The Mystery of a Hansom Cab," "Tracked by a Tattoo," "The Carbuncle Clue." Chapters I–XXVI.

**Ch I Diana on a Bicycle:** July noon, bridge over railway 2 mi from Canterbury. Dora Carew (tall, gold curls, gray eyes, aquiline nose, "modern Diana on a bicycle") waits on fence. Dr. Allen Scott arrives late; her lover, son of Edermont's oldest friend (Dr. Scott senior, died when Allen was 5). Allen treated Lady Burville (guest at Hernwood Hall, Sir Harry Hernwood) who fainted in Chillum Church; Edermont also fainted there during Litany prayer "From battle and murder, and from sudden death, good Lord, deliver us." Edermont shut in room, repeats "Laura Burville." Pallant (red-haired, blue-eyed) is another guest, sent for Allen. Red House: high brick wall, locked gate, locked postern. Joad lives in cottage across road; leaves at nine nightly. Pride (chubby schoolmaster, lookalike of Edermont) is Joad's companion. Cook/servant Meg Gance.

**Ch II Strange Behaviour of Dr. Scott:** Lambert Joad: short, stout, near 60, red bluish face, watery pale eyes, rusty black, white ribbon collar, unsuccessful Anglican parson, Edermont's college friend, drunk, leers at Dora. Joad says Lady Burville should be asked. Edermont shouts from window "Come upstairs, Allen"; Allen goes up. Edermont later shrieks "He will kill me." Allen flees through gate (Joad leaves it unlocked).

**Ch III To Every Man His Own Fear:** Edermont (small, under 5 ft, noble head, weak mouth) asks "Is the gate locked?" Says Dora's parents sinned; warns her away from Lady Burville ("evil woman"). Dora learns Allen broke engagement. Joad at gate: says Allen will break engagement. Hall clock chimes 2:30. Dora rides to Canterbury.

**Ch IV More Mysteries:** Mrs. Tice (Allen's nurse, now housekeeper, green-doored house near Cathedral). Allen gone to London (went via Selling, 4:26 train). Mrs. Tice shows Dora Edermont's photo from a book; recognizes him ("Julian Edermont, twenty years younger"). Mrs. Tice fears "if he should have learnt the truth"; says "you will never become the wife of Allen Scott."

**Ch V Mr. Edermont's High Spirits:** A week passes. Study: oak-panelled, bureau, weapons on walls. Pallant visits Edermont (card: "Mr. Augustus Pallant, on behalf of Laura Burville"). Edermont overjoyed ("My nightmare is at an end!") and faints. Joad rude to Dora.

**Ch VI What Happened in the Night:** Pallant tells Dora "Beware of Allen Scott." Allen's letter says he returns Aug 2. Edermont writes letters (to Allen; another to unknown). Night of Aug 2: Dora's toothache; Edermont: "Allen will tell you." Dora goes to bed. Wakes to cry for help; hall clock strikes one. Dawn: Meg: "The master is... murdered!" Head "bashed in like a pumpkin."

**Ch VII A Nine Days' Scandal:** Body in study; bureau smashed; Zulu knobkerrie; pistol. Joad arrives early, examines body. Inspector Jedd (pompous; theory: tramp burglar). Allen arrives with doctor; tells Dora he will end engagement; won't give reason ("Edermont told me something which parts us for ever").

**Ch VIII The Will of Julian Edermont:** Inquest in dining room. Witnesses: Meg, Dora (heard cry before clock struck one), Joad (alibi: with Pride till after two; found postern open), Dr. Chambers of Canterbury (death between 12 and 1), Jedd. Verdict: murder by persons unknown. Will read by Mr. Carver (lawyer, Canterbury): Dora gets Red House, 200 a year, provided she lives there and Joad continues; bulk (~£50,000) to whoever discovers and punishes assassin. Manuscript (life story) sealed in bureau.

**Ch IX An Amazing Reward:** Newspapers (Morning Planet) publicize. Dora learns no £500 a year income exists; Carver says money was never there; she is about £8,000 expected? (she had expected ~£8,000). Carver: "find that woman."

**Ch X Dr. Scott Is Still Obstinate:** Dora visits Allen. He refuses; says Edermont's secret parts them; denies Lady Burville has to do with it. Dora asks Mrs. Tice to come stay at Red House.

**Ch XI Preparing the Ground:** Mrs. Tice moves in. Dora tricks Mrs. Tice: Mrs. Tice admits knowing Edermont before. Dora deduces Edermont = false name; Christchurch, Hants. Mrs. Tice's husband died 25 years ago, buried at Christchurch Priory. Mrs. Tice not in love with Edermont.

**Ch XII A Terrible Accusation:** Dora feigns affection for Joad; Joad drunk, confesses hints; Joad proposes marriage, says he knows who killed Julian; accuses Allen. Joad claims he saw Allen on bicycle near Red House past midnight, went in via postern. Gives Dora one week; threatens denunciation.

**Ch XIII Denial:** Dora goes to Allen in Canterbury; Allen admits he was at Red House at midnight by Edermont's letter, found body dead, fled. Mentions woman on bicycle who got punctured tyre near railway bridge, later he finds pearl brooch "L.B." (Laura Burville) in study.

**Ch XIV What Dr. Scott Saw:** Allen describes scene (candle, Zulu club, pistol). Meeting woman on road, mended her tyre with gutta-percha.

**Ch XV The Pearl Brooch:** Dora takes brooch. Sir Harry gives Lady Burville's address (No. 22 Jersey Place, Mayfair). Dora goes to London next day.

**Ch XVI Dora Is Startled:** On train, Pride (Mallison in disguise) rides with her; says he met two cyclists on road Canterbury–Chillum that night (man towards Chillum, woman towards Canterbury). Lady Burville at Jersey Place: "I am your mother."

**Ch XVII A Story of the Past:** Lady Burville (born Laura Treherne), first married Captain George Theophilus Carew (sea captain, violent, jealous); after 6 months he was reported lost. She married Julian Dargill (= Edermont) and had Dora. Carew survived, returned, sought Dargill; Dargill fled to America, then gave Laura an annuity to take Dora. Laura married Sir John Burville. Pallant blackmailed her 2 years. She says Carew killed Dargill.

**Ch XVIII Pallant Makes a Statement:** Dora extracts promise of silence from Lady Burville. Joad jealous; Dora returns home. Pallant calls next morning: Carew died in San Francisco in Pallant's arms, years earlier; Pallant told Carew's story. Mrs. Tice alarmed at Dora's visit to London.

**Ch XIX More Mysteries:** Pallant insists burglary theory, notes clock "might have been wrong." Dora's clock was set right before she slept. Pallant warns Joad. Mrs. Tice says Allen ill; Dora will go over with Mrs. Tice.

**Ch XX The Sins of the Father:** Mrs. Tice tells the past: Dr. Scott (Allen's father) had flirted with Laura; Carew, returning, shot Dr. Scott at the drawing-room French window believing him to be Dargill, who had been sent for. Mrs. Tice was Allen's nurse since infancy (his mother died at his birth).

**Ch XXI So Near, and Yet So Far:** Dora says she can never marry Allen. At Allen's sickbed (dining-room sofa) Dora tells him Lady Burville is her mother; Allen reveals Edermont's letters etc. Allen went to London, read *Morning Planet* report of the 1870s-ish double homicide (Carew shot Dr. Scott). Allen speculates Pallant/letters.

**Ch XXII What Dora Discovered:** Meg says hall clock was an hour fast the morning after (ten vs nine). Dora searches Joad's cottage (back-door key under water-butt). Finds "The Confession of Julian Dargill, better known as Julian Edermont" in fireplace ash.

**Ch XXIII The Madness of Lambert Joad:** Joad discovers manuscript gone, rages, goes to Carver in Canterbury. Dora confronts Carver: Carver to detain Joad.

**Ch XXIV The Stolen Manuscript:** Manuscript read: Julian Dargill born Christchurch; friend John Mallison (rake, clever); loved Laura Burville (Treherne); rivals Dr. Scott (widower) and Captain Carew. Carew married Laura; wreck of *Silver Arrow* off Guinea; Laura widowed; Dargill married her; Dora born; Carew returned, killed Dr. Scott by mistake; Dargill fled; Mallison took his name and fled to America; Dargill took name Edermont and bought Red House via Carver; Dora (his daughter) sent to him by Laura. Dora = Dargill's daughter, not Carew's.

**Ch XXV Confession:** Mrs. Tice told; Allen and Dora rejoice. Carver arrives: Joad gave sworn confession (accessory after fact); Joad alibi was made by Mallison-in-disguise. Pallant's demand for letters; Edermont invited Lady Burville and Scott at midnight to resolve. Joad altered clock by an hour; hid behind door; Mallison (= Pride) came, quarrelled, struck Edermont with knobkerrie; Joad hid manuscript. Pride = John Mallison.

**Ch XXVI A Final Surprise:** Joad dies of heart failure on doorstep on night of Pride's arrest; Joad left £50,000 to Dora. Mallison confesses night before execution; executed. Pallant later shot in San Francisco gambling house. Lady Burville confessed to Sir John; Sir John remarried her. Dora & Allen to marry in spring; Dora inherits £50,000 from Joad; Carver: "Hear, hear!"

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE TOP OF THE WORLD (Ethel M. Dell, 1920, Gutenberg 12360)

**Front:** Dedication to mother; poem ("When you have reached the top of the world... by faith and love and God's goodness"). Four Parts; chapters numbered per part.

**Part I Ch I Advice:** Sylvia Ingleton (tawny/red-brown hair, red-brown eyes), daughter of Squire Gilbert Ingleton of the Manor; head gardener Jeffcott. Her love Guy Ranger (son of squire's bailiff, Ranger yeomen; public-school educated) banished 5 years earlier to South Africa cousin's farm; promised to return. Father has married Mrs. Emmott (= Caroline), a widow, grasping. Sylvia's inheritance at 25.

**Ch II The New Mistress:** Mrs. Ingleton (Caroline, tall, handsome, domineering; "Madam"). Neighbour Captain George Preston, M.F.H., rich, wants Sylvia; crude, "Cherry-ripe."

**Ch III The Whip-Hand:** Mrs. Ingleton: "I have the whip-hand." Sylvia rides with squire; refuses to call stepmother Mother; leaves room.

**Ch IV The Victor:** Hunt Ball. Preston presses; Vernon Eversley. Sylvia, exhausted, agrees to be "provisionally engaged" to Preston if no word from Guy.

**Ch V The Miracle:** Sylvia learns Jeffcott saw a South African letter from Guy arrive; Mrs. Ingleton had suppressed Guy's letters. Sylvia confronts her; leaves for Guy; squire lets her go. Preston's dismissal.

**Ch VI The Land of Strangers:** Ritzen station, South Africa. Guy not there; "Burke Ranger" (Guy's cousin, rancher at Blue Hill Farm) meets her. Guy is drinking, ill (delirium tremens). Burke: "go back and marry someone else."

**Ch VII The Wrong Turning:** Burke says Guy "taken the wrong turning." Sylvia asks to see Guy; Burke takes her by cart. She promises not to marry Guy as way out.

**Ch VIII The Comrade:** Long cart ride; Ritter Spruit; picnic; Sylvia calls herself "partner"; Burke's cart; sleeping on veldt. Storm; they reach farm, Mary Ann (old Kaffir woman), Joe, Fair Rosamond; Diamond horse (gift). Burke sleeps in separate room; Sylvia in guest room.

**Ch IX The Arrival:** Sylvia leaves Burke's hut; Guy is absent; Burke says Guy "cleared out." Kieff (doctor, swarthy, onyx eyes) mentioned.

**Ch X The Dream:** Recurring dream: two horsemen collide on ravine path; one falls.

**Ch XI The Cross-Roads:** Sylvia sees Guy's hut at the spruit; Piet Vreiboom (Boer, leering) sees her; Burke says she's his wife. Burke proposes marriage; Sylvia agrees on terms of comradeship ("partner"). Skeleton tree; "Fide et Amore" carved.

**Ch XII The Stale:** Civil marriage at Brennerstadt. Race to skeleton tree; Burke carves words.

**Part II Ch I Comrades:** Blue Hill Farm life; Sylvia overseer; Burke whips Joe; they visit Guy's abandoned hut.

**Ch II The Visitors:** Merstons (Bill, red-faced; Matilda, bitter, six dead children) visit.

**Ch III The Bargain:** Sylvia, on the kopje, hears Burke's feelings; she asks him to rescue Guy; Burke: "a bargain."

**Ch IV The Capture:** Donovan Kelly (Irish, diamond mine manager) helps Burke take Guy from Hoffstein's bar, Brennerstadt.

**Ch V The Good Cause:** Burke breaks Guy's will; Burke's inner monologue about faith and love.

**Ch VI The Return:** Sylvia prepares hut for Guy; Burke returns late, unshaven-cut chin; kisses Sylvia.

**Ch VII The Guest:** Guy visits, drinks; coughs; Sylvia and Guy reunite.

**Ch VIII The Interruption:** Guy shoots himself (attempt); Burke takes revolver. Kieff summoned.

**Ch IX The Abyss:** Guy's near-death; Sylvia comforts.

**Ch X The Desire to Live:** Kieff, morphine; Burke enraged.

**Ch XI The Remedy:** Guy recovers; Kieff's morphia; Burke confronts Sylvia about morphia.

**Part III Ch I The New Era:** Sylvia becomes morphia-addicted via Kieff. Burke sends Kieff away.

**Ch II Into Battle:** Burke asserts mastery; Sylvia defies, then yields.

**Ch III The Seed:** Mrs. Merston's friendship with Sylvia.

**Ch IV Mirage:** Sylvia strikes Fair Rosamond; Guy's declarations.

**Ch V Everybody's Friend:** Veldt fire; Kelly visits; Burke kisses Sylvia.

**Ch VI The Hero:** Burke and Guy fight fire; Guy saves Burke. Sylvia gives Guy drink.

**Ch VII The Net:** Guy's passion; Sylvia refuses.

**Ch VIII The Summons:** Merston injured; Burke leaves to help.

**Ch IX For the Sake of the Old Love:** Sylvia finds Burke's strong-box key; Guy took money (diamond gamble, Wilbraham's diamond raffle).

**Ch X The Bearer of Evil Tidings:** Kieff tells Kelly Sylvia left with Guy.

**Ch XI The Sharp Corner:** Sylvia rides to Brennerstadt, finds Burke at hotel.

**Ch XII The Cost:** Burke's accusation; Sylvia's "I am yours."

**Part IV Ch I Sand of the Desert:** Burke and Kelly; Sylvia refuses to give up searching for Guy.

**Ch II The Skeleton Tree:** Sylvia confides in Kelly; sees "Fide et Amore" on tree.

**Ch III The Punishment:** Burke beats Kieff publicly in Brennerstadt; Kieff apologises; Sylvia collapses.

**Ch IV The Evil Thing:** Kieff dies by overdose.

**Ch V The Land of Blasted Hopes:** Return to farm; Sylvia returns money to strong-box.

**Ch VI The Parting:** Burke takes Sylvia to Merstons; kisses her farewell.

**Ch VII Piet Vreiboom:** Sylvia's friendship with Matilda; Piet's visit; Sylvia's letter.

**Ch VIII Out of the Depths:** Guy comes to Sylvia at night; attacks; Sylvia helps him with injection.

**Ch IX The Meeting:** Burke rides to confront Guy in hut.

**Ch X The Truth:** Burke tells Matilda Sylvia loves Guy.

**Ch XI The Storm:** Drought; Burke's despair; cloudburst.

**Ch XII The Sacrifice:** Burke rescues Sylvia and Guy from the flood; Guy dies later on horse.

**Ch XIII By Faith and Love:** Guy dies; Burke and Sylvia reconcile; diamond left to them; they stand on kopje.
